subject: Very simple example of debugging issue with Probabilistic syntax

messages.author: 8f1ef4d67aa2033e
messages.subject: Very simple example of debugging issue with Probabilistic syntax
parts:
Hello,
I'm new to using the syntax but familiar with TMB. I was having trouble debugging some code and located the issue. In the code below, any thoughts on why simply adding the probabilistic print statement seem to mess up the estimation but the other way doesn't.
Thanks to anyone who knows,
Brandon

set.seed(10)
data <- list(x = rbinom(100,1,prob=0.2))
parameters <- list(mu = 0)
f <- function(parms){
  RTMB::getAll(data,
               parms)
  x <- OBS(x)
  # print(x[1]%~%RTMB::dbinom(1,plogis(mu)))
  # print(RTMB::dbinom(1,1,plogis(mu),log=TRUE))
  nll <- -sum(dbinom(x,1,plogis(mu),log=TRUE))
  return(nll)
}
obj <- RTMB::MakeADFun(f,
                       parameters,
                       silent = FALSE)
opt <- nlminb(obj$par,
              obj$fn,
              obj$gr)
print(opt$par)

messages.author: 361e593259030741
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Very simple example of debugging issue with Probabilistic syntax
parts:
Hi, Brandon.
The line looks suspicious, which is "nll <- -sum(dbinom(x,1,plogis(mu),log=TRUE))."    Usually the folks do its calculation as follows:

Type nll = 0.0; 
for(int i=0; i<n; i++)  {
  ......
  nll -= dbinom(x(i),1,plogis(mu),log=TRUE));
};

Hope this helps.  Cheers,
Saang-Yoon

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Very simple example of debugging issue with Probabilistic syntax
parts:
Hi Saang-Yoon,
Thanks for the quick response. The likelihood is fine: it's simply summing instead of doing the incrementing. The problem, I think, stems from the probabilistic syntax that was added to the RTMB package. For some reason, simply adding print(1%~%binom(1,par)) seems to blow up the estimation, even though it's not part of the likelihood. I'm sure it's just my unfamiliarity with the new syntax.
Brandon

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Very simple example of debugging issue with Probabilistic syntax
parts:
I'm not entirely sure I understand the problem, but it seems you expect this line (???):
x[1] %~% RTMB::dbinom(1,plogis(mu))
to be equivalent with
nll <- -sum(dbinom(x,1,plogis(mu),log=TRUE))

However, that looks like a typo. It should have been:
x %~% RTMB::dbinom(1,plogis(mu))
